patients.summary: Retired landscape architect with a mechanical aortic valve, atrial fibrillation on warfarin, insulin-treated type 2 diabetes and coronary disease after a 2012 inferior MI. Joins in 2018; pulmonary TB in 2022 complicates warfarin dosing and brings a minor bleed; inferior STEMIs in 2023 and 2025 (the second after his last visit, with RV involvement).

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Howland phoned about joining. His internist of many years is retiring at the end of the month. Medicare. Sees an outside cardiology group for his heart valve and atrial fibrillation; their anticoagulation clinic handles his warfarin. Membership agreement emailed. New patient slot given for 9/18 at 9:20. Asked him to sign a release so we can get his old office's chart, and to bring all his pill bottles and his insulin pen.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66M, retired landscape architect, transferring care; his longtime internist is retiring.

Cardiac history is the bulk of it. Born with a bicuspid aortic valve (a brother has one too); it became stenotic and he had a mechanical aortic valve put in this past March. Atrial fibrillation on top of that, rate controlled on metoprolol. Inferior STEMI in 2012 with a stent to the right coronary; he stopped smoking that year after about 30 pack-years. Followed by an outside cardiology group. Their anticoagulation clinic doses his warfarin (goal 2.5-3.5); he gets fingersticks there every few weeks and says the numbers have been steady since surgery.

Diabetes for years, on metformin and glargine 24 units at night. Checks sugars mornings, mostly 120s-150s. No lows. BP checked at the cardiology visits, told it was fine.

Meds (bottles reviewed): warfarin 7.5 mg daily per clinic, metoprolol succinate 100, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, glargine 24 u qhs, atorvastatin 40.
Allergies: none to drugs.
Family: father MI at 62. Mother type 2 diabetes. Brother bicuspid valve.
Social: retired from landscape design, still keeps up a big garden. Ex-smoker as above. Alcohol maybe once a month or less.
ROS: no chest pain since the stent, no palpitations lately, no bleeding or bruising beyond the usual, no claudication, no foot numbness.

Exam: well, unhurried. Vitals as charted. Healed sternotomy. Irregularly irregular rhythm with a crisp mechanical closing click; no new murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt throughout, pulses present.
ECG here: AF, rate controlled, old inferior Q waves.

A/P
1. Mechanical AVR, AF, on warfarin - managed by cardiology's anticoag clinic. Asked them to copy us on INR reports.
2. CAD, old inferior MI, RCA stent - no angina. Same beta blocker and statin.
3. T2DM on insulin - A1c, UACR today. Eye exam due; he has an optometrist.
4. HTN - acceptable today.
5. HLD - lipids today.
6. Health maintenance: hep C and HIV screen once. Former heavy smoker - low-dose CT for lung screening and a one-time AAA ultrasound ordered. Old office says colonoscopy around 2015; will confirm in records. Flu and pneumococcal next month at a nurse visit.
Records release signed. Back in about 3 months.

documents.title: Your new-patient bloodwork
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Howland, your labs from Tuesday look reasonable. A1c 7.6 - a bit above where we'd aim, but not far, and no change needed yet. Kidney function and urine protein are normal. Cholesterol about what I'd expect on atorvastatin 40. Hep C and HIV screens negative. Blood counts normal. I'll see you in December.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received 62 pages from the patient's former internal medicine office, covering 2009-2018.

Problem list there: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, coronary artery disease with inferior MI 2012 (RCA stent), hyperlipidemia, atrial fibrillation, bicuspid aortic valve with stenosis, s/p mechanical aortic valve replacement March 2018. Former smoker, quit 2012.
Medications match what he brought to his first visit.
Screening: colonoscopy 2015 - normal, no polyps. No drug allergies listed.
Cardiac surgery operative summary (March 2018): bicuspid aortic valve, severe calcific stenosis, replaced with a mechanical prosthesis; uneventful recovery.
2012 catheterization summary: inferior STEMI, culprit right coronary artery, one stent.

Filed. PCP to review.

documents.title: Nurse visit - immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu L deltoid, PCV13 R deltoid. On warfarin - fine-gauge needle, firm pressure 2 min each site, no hematoma. Tolerated well. PPSV23 due in a year.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Indication: lung cancer screening, former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 2012. Technique: low-dose non-contrast CT of the chest. Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Lungs clear. Airways patent. No pleural effusion. Postoperative sternotomy wires and a mechanical aortic valve prosthesis. Coronary stent in the right coronary artery. Heart size normal. No adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Annual screening in 12 months.

reports.text: Indication: AAA screening. Abdominal aorta normal in caliber throughout, maximum diameter 2.1 cm. No aneurysm. Iliac origins unremarkable. Visualized liver and kidneys unremarkable.

documents.title: Screening CT and aorta ultrasound
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lung screening CT clean, Lung-RADS 1; repeat next fall. Aorta normal size - no further AAA screening. Portal note sent.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing fine. Raking and splitting wood without chest symptoms. Morning sugars 120-160. Anticoag clinic has kept him on 7.5 mg daily; last INR there 2.9 per his card. Old records reviewed - colonoscopy 2015 normal, op note consistent with his account.
O: Vitals as charted. Rhythm irregular, rate fine, valve click crisp. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P: T2DM - A1c today, glargine unchanged for now. HTN controlled. AF/mechanical AVR stable on warfarin through cardiology. Return March.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 7.5, a hair better than September. Kidney function and potassium normal. No changes - see you in March.

documents.title: Insulin glargine pen refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request for glargine pens, last filled by prior internist. 24 units nightly, 5 pens per 30 days plus pen needles. Sent per PCP standing refill protocol, 90-day supply with 3 refills.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter was quiet. Walking at the mall most mornings. No chest pain, no palpitations he notices, no lightheadedness. Glucose log mostly under 150. No hypoglycemia.
Exam: as charted. Irregular rhythm, mechanical click. Lungs clear. Feet intact.
Plan: A1c drawn. No med changes. Tdap and first Shingrix today; second Shingrix in 2-6 months. RTC June.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 7.4 - drifting in the right direction. Keep doing what you're doing.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Optometry report, dilated exam 05/07/2019. Patient: William Howland. Diabetes on insulin. Allergies: NKDA.
Visual acuity correctable to 20/25 OU. IOP normal. Lens: early age-appropriate changes. Fundus: no diabetic retinopathy either eye, no macular edema.
Recall one year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Brief visit. Garden in full swing, working most mornings before the heat. Arm sore for a day or two after the first Shingrix, nothing more. No bleeding issues on warfarin.
BP fine. Heart irregular, click present. No edema.
Second Shingrix today. BMP for lisinopril. Next: wellness visit in September.

documents.title: Anticoagulation clinic INR summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Anticoagulation clinic summary, outside cardiology group. Indication: mechanical aortic valve, atrial fibrillation. Goal INR 2.5-3.5. Warfarin 7.5 mg daily, unchanged.
Recent fingerstick INRs: 06/04 2.7, 07/02 3.1, 07/30 2.9.
No bleeding reported. Allergies: NKDA. Next check 4 weeks.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Medicare annual wellness visit, first one here.
Function: independent in all ADLs and IADLs. Drives. No falls this year. Hearing and vision adequate with glasses. Cognition: three-word recall 3/3, clock normal.
Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Safety: seat belt, smoke detectors, no firearms in the house.
Advance directive: has a health care proxy on file with his lawyer; will bring a copy.
Preventive: Tdap 3/2019, Shingrix series done, PCV13 last fall - PPSV23 due now (nurse visit with flu). Colonoscopy 2015 normal. Lung CT due next month. AAA screen done. Hep C/HIV done.
Chronic: no chest pain, no palpitations he notices, garden work without breathlessness. Sugars steady.
Exam: vitals as charted. Irregular rhythm, crisp valve click, lungs clear, no edema. Feet - normal sensation, no lesions.
Labs drawn. Personalized prevention plan given.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from your wellness visit: A1c 7.3, kidney and liver tests normal, blood counts normal, urine protein normal. LDL about the same as last year on atorvastatin. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Nurse visit - flu and PPSV23
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high dose) L arm, PPSV23 R arm. Pressure held on both, no bleeding. Pneumococcal series now complete. Reminded about lung CT on the 24th.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Comparison: 10/25/2018. Technique: low-dose non-contrast chest CT. Findings: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation. No effusion. Mechanical aortic valve and sternotomy wires again noted. Coronary stent. No adenopathy.

documents.title: Lung screening CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative again. Annual screening continues. Patient notified via portal.

documents.title: Office visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seasonal check-in. Holiday eating has started; sugars a little higher in the evenings. Otherwise no complaints. Cardiology visit this past summer was routine by his report.
Exam unchanged - irregular rhythm with click, lungs clear, feet fine.
A1c today. Talked portion sizes and keeping up the walks over winter. No medication changes. Next visit in early spring.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 7.5, up slightly with the holidays as we expected. Recheck in spring.
